name: Toronto

character.name: Rocco the raccoon

intro.text: Oh hey, new face on my block. Everybody round here, I know. So, let's see if you're from Trawna.

outro.text: Okay, okay. Let's see where you're at, bud.

character.voice: ElevenLabs Voice Design: friendly, laid-back Toronto man in his thirties, standard Canadian English, warm and a little sly

im from trawna

test.tip: Two beats, not three: "TRAW-na". Let the second T disappear, like locals do.

good.text: Trawna! Okay, okay, I hear you.

bad.text: Three whole syllables? That's the airport announcement, bud.

test.line: Let's head out and about, eh?
test.meaning: Let's go out and walk around, right?
accepted: let's head out and about eh
lets head out and about eh
let's head out and about
lets head out and about
let's head out and about a
let's head out and about hey
let's head out and about ay
test.tip: In "out" and "about" start the vowel a bit higher, closer to "uh-oot" than "ow". Not "a boot"! Then lift "eh?" up at the end.

good.text: Out and about, eh! That's the real thing.

ok.text: Good. Start the "out" a little higher, "uh-oot".

bad.text: That's "ow-t". Nobody says it like that around here.

test.line: Say less, fam. Mans is on the way, ahlie.
test.meaning: Got it, friend. I'm on my way, for real.
accepted: say less fam mans is on the way ahlie

test.tip: Even, punchy beats: "SAY LESS. FAM." Then "mans" means "I" here. Finish with a quick "ah-lie?", like "right?".

ok.text: Not bad. Keep the beats even and quick.

bad.text: "Mans"? You said it like a sentence from a textbook.

celebration.text: Total tourist! Don't worry, we'll get you sounding like Trawna.
Not bad! You're a proper visitor now, eh.
Okay! You could get a place on my street.
Say less. You're from the 6ix, no question.

items.line: Grab your toque, it's cold out.
items.meaning: Grab your winter hat, it's cold outside.

items.tip: "Toque" rhymes with "duke", short: "took". And "out" starts high: "uh-oot".

good.text: Toque on. You're ready for February.

bad.text: A toke?! No, no. A toque. The hat.

items.line: Can I get a medium double-double?
items.meaning: Can I have a medium coffee with two cream and two sugar?

ok.text: Sure. Bit more relaxed, it's just coffee.

bad.text: A what? Oh, a double-double. Okay, sure.

good.text: Bare cold, ahlie. You get it.

setting: Low-poly Toronto street on a crisp autumn day: red-brick Victorian houses with bay windows, a corner store with an awning, a red streetcar at its stop, a small park basketball court, maple trees and a generic downtown skyline with a tall needle tower silhouette, no brands.
